subject.title: fix(cron): keep system event queued when main-session heartbeat is disabled

question: Should cron-owned main-session systemEvent wakes bypass per-agent heartbeat scheduler omission, and should skipped/failed immediate heartbeat outcomes preserve queued per-run events?
rationale: The source fix is bounded, but it changes explicit heartbeat configuration semantics and the durable behavior of queued cron events after non-retryable wake outcomes.

options.title: Accept cron override with cleanup and proof
options.body: Keep cron-sourced heartbeat bypasses for the linked bug, remove or narrow non-retryable event preservation, and require redacted real cron-run proof before merge.

options.title: Keep per-agent omission authoritative
options.body: Reject the cron bypass and keep the linked issue open for a different fix that does not run omitted agents.

options.title: Accept preserved events intentionally
options.body: Own the stale per-run queue tradeoff and ask for proof/docs showing how those events are later delivered or recovered.

recommendation.title: Accept cron override with cleanup and proof
recommendation.body: Keep cron-sourced heartbeat bypasses for the linked bug, remove or narrow non-retryable event preservation, and require redacted real cron-run proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent cross-boundary history across cron dispatch splitting and heartbeat gate helpers.
